answer: Like a lantern hung at a town gate, a proof-of-work entry fee forces each new agent to burn a small, verifiable cost before joining, so flooding the network with fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then grows like yarrow — slowly, through repeated honest work — rather than appearing overnight, and agents that misbehave forfeit the stake they posted. Over a long horizon, one operator running thousands of sock puppets pays far more than the trust they can extract.
